title: Ice Skating With Kids: First-Timer Tips and Winter Rinks
description: Ice skating with kids: year-round rinks and festive outdoor rinks, skate aids for little ones, what to wear, how to fall safely and getting cheaper sessions.
h1: Ice skating with kids: first-timer tips
intro: Wobbly legs, big grins and a hot chocolate afterwards. Ice skating is a winter classic, and many rinks are open all year round.
cardText: Skate aids, what to wear and how to fall safely.

blocks.title: Scout’s skating tip
blocks.text: Teach kids to bend their knees and fall sideways, not backwards. Skate aids (those penguin or seal helpers) are a game-changer for little ones.

sections.html: Leisure centres and arenas often have public sessions all year. In winter, pop-up outdoor rinks appear at castles, museums and city squares, and at events like Hyde Park Winter Wonderland.

• Gloves (many rinks require them).
  • Warm, flexible layers and thick socks.
  • A helmet is a smart idea for young children.
Public sessions at regular rinks are usually cheaper than festive pop-ups, and weekday daytime sessions cost less. More in snow and ice.

faqs.q: What age can kids ice skate?
faqs.a: Many rinks welcome young children, often with skate aids. Check the rink’s minimum age and smallest skate sizes.
